original_value: In this study, we develop a vegetation monitoring framework which is applicable at a planetary scale, and is based on the BACI (Before-After, Control-Impact) design. This approach utilizes Google Earth Engine, a state-of-the-art cloud computing platform. A web-based application for users named EcoDash was developed. EcoDash maps vegetation using Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) from Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) products (the MOD13A1 and MYD13A1 collections) from both Terra and Aqua sensors from the years 2000 and 2002, respectively. to detect change in vegetation, we define an EVI baseline period, and then draw results at a planetary scale using the web-based application by measuring improvement or degradation in vegetation based on the user-defined baseline periods. We also used EcoDash to measure the impact of deforestation and mitigation efforts by the Vietnam Forests and Deltas (VFD) program for the Nghe An and Thanh Hoa provinces in Vietnam. Using the period before 2012 as a baseline, we found that as of March 2017, 86% of the geographical area within the VFD program shows improvement, compared to only a 24% improvement in forest cover for all of Vietnam. Overall, we show how using satellite imagery for monitoring vegetation in a cloud-computing environment could be a cost-effective and useful tool for land managers and other practitioners

result.paraphrase: This study presents a planetary-scale vegetation monitoring framework built on the BACI (Before-After, Control-Impact) design. It uses Google Earth Engine, a leading cloud-computing platform, and a user-facing web application called EcoDash. EcoDash maps vegetation with Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) data from MODIS products, specifically the MOD13A1 and MYD13A1 collections, using Terra and Aqua sensor observations from 2000 and 2002, respectively. To detect vegetation change, we establish an EVI baseline period and then present planetary-scale results through the web application by assessing vegetation improvement or degradation relative to user-defined baseline periods. We also applied EcoDash to evaluate the effects of deforestation and mitigation activities under the Vietnam Forests and Deltas (VFD) program in the Nghe An and Thanh Hoa provinces of Vietnam. Using the period before 2012 as the baseline, we found that by March 2017, 86% of the area within the VFD program showed improvement, versus only 24% improvement in forest cover across Vietnam as a whole. Overall, we demonstrate that satellite imagery for vegetation monitoring in a cloud-computing setting can be a cost-effective and valuable tool for land managers and other practitioners
